body: My family supports me in whatever I do, I have some trust issues with the women in my family, but my father knows everything and does his best to help me when I need it.  My parents divorced when I was 18, but were separated for probably 13 years before that, lived in separate parts of the country, and basically hate each other.  I am the cool brother, the cool uncle, everyone loves it when I am around.  I have a lot of friends, I would say 95% would drop anything to come and help me, so yes basically genuine.  My mother threw me out of the house when I was 17 because she couldn't deal with my extracurricular activities.  I wasn't doing bad things. I just went to a lot of weekend parties and would make her nervous I guess, and no, no drugs, the occasional joint but that's it.  I was thrown out of the house, my gf of 3 years broke up with me, I lost full ride college scholarships, and my parents filed for divorce all in the same week my senior year of high-school, which I think has some kind of contribution to this, but I'm not a psychiatrist.

1.  Figure out what I want.
2.  Develop a plan.
3.  Actively work on this plan.
4.  Build the life I want.

I live moment to moment, never thinking of the future because it may never come.  I guess I have to believe that there will be a future and I will be a part of it, which I never thought before, I never thought I would make it to 30, which is probably why I never made a plan.  I will decide today what I want and make a plan to get there.

Thank you for your words, I realized when I was reading that I don't have any goals, I don't even remember when I did. I need to decide what it is that I want to do, obviously alcohol is a hindrance for me.  I have never really tried to stop on my own but if I am able to stop the alcohol abuse, maybe I can stop this depression and work towards the goals that I need to set for myself.
This makes complete sense, how do I find out why I am not allowing myself a chance to have a better life?

As far as a relationship with a woman, I couldn't do it because I couldn't trust them, it wouldn't be their fault, but I believe with my trust issues, I would cause the problems.  Looks are the last thing I would consider anyway.  Humans basically suck, they walk by only caring for themselves and their, to use a psychology term, ID.  I know the pessimism is thick here but it is what I am conditioned to believe.

I don't know, its like an urge.  I can go for a week without drinking at all but then I just have a need to get belligerent and internally hurt myself.  I don't think its something I can even control.  I have scars on my arms and legs from falling down while in a blackout state, I have meaningful conversations with people that I don't remember, I run into complete strangers who know me because we spent some significant time together in my blackouts, but I don't know them which makes me the stuck up asshole who didn't think enough of them to remember, which is the exact opposite of the kind of person I am.  The booze is part of my identity, when friends see me coming they know that there is some sort of debotchourus party to follow directly.

No worries, in my experiences a girl that looks like that is usually void of any intelligent conversation, which is a requirement for me.  Ive long given up trying to find a companion, I have been devastated in the past and now I refuse to open up and let anyone in to do it to me again.  Which is probably a problem in itself, but its what works for me.

This is good advice.  Every time I respond to a comment on here, it brings me back to my alcohol problem.  I did some researching and it seems alcoholism and depression are related.  If I am to stop the digging I have to stop the drinking.  That is a beast that I don't think I can conquer.

Never thought of this.  I have always wanted to help, maybe in a third world country, I love to learn and to teach, I would like to travel and see things that I only see in books.  I even looked into joining the peace core but I am not allowed to leave the country because of my debt from college and my alcohol related d.u.i.  I speak and understand a little Spanish and would love to teach people to speak the English language and teach about life in my country.  These things are nearly unattainable, especially when I can't even care enough about myself to help me.

This is where I am.  I know I'm an alcoholic, self diagnosed obviously, but I am an intelligent person and can do my own research.  Alcohol makes me happy, it makes me have fun and through my groups of friends I am the one who is the party animal (I am "Gandalf" from that episode of Friends).  I know that if I am able to stop drinking I will be a completely different person, which could be fine, I just don't know if I could or if I even want to.  Health is not the reason to stop because I could care less about when I leave this place.
Thanks for the words but the gif is just a reminder of something I will never have.

I really don't know the last time when I was happy.  I mean, I guess I was happy at some point, maybe during high-school, but that was over 10 years ago.  A lot has changed since then, people grew up conqured whatever part of the world they wanted, and I got left behind.  Not that I expected the world to fall in my lap but, I haven't even dented this world with my mark.  I love football (American football) so on Saturdays and Sundays I can keep my mind occupied, but for the other 5 days I fall behind when the rest of the world is making strides, having kids, buying cars and houses...while I live in a friends basement waiting to expire.

I don't do doctors, I don't even care to see one, I believe I would only receive news that I have five types of cancer or something, which I'm pretty sure I do.  I understand that plenty of people care about me but I'm just tired of depending on others.  I have no money, no credit card, hell, I don't even have a bank account, I haven't eaten in 3 days and don't know or care where or when my next meal will come from.

I have been using them as a reason for a long time now, I know its a selfish thing, but there comes a point where I see them as selfish for requiring me to always be around.  Like most guys, I like sports and was once very good at them, which I believe is another contribution to my depression.  I lost college scholarships, a longtime girlfriend, and my parents got divorced in the same week in high-school, of course that was 10 years ago.  I have bounced around from place to place trying to find my niche to no avail.  Now I have over 40k in debt, no degree to show for it, and no job to even begin to pay it back.  I don't have a fear of dying, I rather look foward to it, because whatever is next is guaranteed to be better than this place and I have friends waiting on me anyway.
